articles.text: XUÉSHENG: Táng Xiānsheng, wǒ kěyi jìnlai ma?
STUDENT: Professor Táng, may I come in?
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Dāngrán, qǐng jìnlai ba! Yǒu shì ma?
PROFESSOR TÁNG: Of course, please come in! Is there something you want to see me about?
XUÉSHENG: Mm, jīntian shàng kède shíhou nín dàgài hěn bù shūfu, wǒ lái kànkan nín.
STUDENT: Um, in class today you must have felt very bad, so I've come to see you.
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Ou! Hái dàile huār lai! Xièxie ni.
PROFESSOR TÁNG: Oh! You even brought flowers! Thank you.
XUÉSHENG: Méi shenme, yīnggāide. Táng Xiānsheng, nín xiànzàide gǎnjué zěnmeyàng, hǎo yìdiǎnr ma?
STUDENT: Not at all, it's only proper. Professor Táng, how do you feel now — better?
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Hǎoduō le, xièxie ni.
PROFESSOR TÁNG: Much better, thank you.
XUÉSHENG: Yǒu shénme wǒ kěyi gěi nín zuòde... nín bié kèqi.
STUDENT: If there's anything I can do for you... don't be polite.
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Nǐ qù dào liǎngbēi kāfēi lai, hǎo bu hǎo?
PROFESSOR TÁNG: How about going and pouring us a couple of cups of coffee?
XUÉSHENG: Wǒ xiǎng, jīntian shàng kède shíhou nín tài jīdòng, xiànzài zuì hǎo bù hē kāfēi.
STUDENT: I think that during class today you got too worked up. It would be best if you didn't have any coffee now.
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Hǎo ba, nǐ dào liǎngbēi júzishuǐ lai. Wǒ bú yào bīng.
PROFESSOR TÁNG: Okay, then get us two glasses of orange juice. I don't want any ice.
XUÉSHENG: Hǎode, wǒ jiù lái.
STUDENT: Okay, I'll be right back.
XUÉSHENG: Táng Xiānsheng, yǒu yíjù huà wǒ bù zhīdào kěyi bu kěyi shuō.
STUDENT: Professor Táng, there's something I want to say but I don't know if I can.
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Yǒu shénme huà, nǐ jiù shuō ba!
PROFESSOR TÁNG: Whatever you have to say, just say it!
XUÉSHENG: Nín měicì jiǎng Zhōngguo liùshí niándài wénxué dōu fēicháng jīdòng, zhèiyàngr duì nínde shēntǐ bù hǎo!
STUDENT: Every time you talk about Chinese literature of the sixties you get very agitated. That's bad for your health!
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Wǒ yě zhīdao, kěshi yì tán zhèi fāngmiànde wèntí, zǒngshi ràng wo hěn jīdòng.
PROFESSOR TÁNG: I know, but as soon as I talk about the topic it always makes me very agitated.
XUÉSHENG: Zhōngguo wénxuéde qíngkuàng zhèijǐnián yǒule hěn dàde gǎibiàn. Yǒude shíhou hǎo yìdiǎnr, yǒude shíhou bù zěnme hǎo.
STUDENT: There have been big changes in the state of Chinese literature in the past few years. Sometimes it's been a little better and sometimes it hasn't been too good.
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Zhōngguóde shìqing jiù shi zhèiyàng, hé zhèngzhìde guānxi tài dà. Wǒ lǎo le, wǒ méi bànfǎ dǒng le.
PROFESSOR TÁNG: That's exactly the way things are in China; their relationship with politics is too great. I'm too old, I can't understand it any more.
XUÉSHENG: Nín shi wǒmende lǎoshī. Rúguǒ nín bù dǒng, shéi dǒng ne?
STUDENT: But you're our teacher. If you don't understand, who does?
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Āi, yǐhòude yánjiū, jiù shi nǐmen niánqīng rénde shì le.
PROFESSOR TÁNG: In the future, research will be the job of you young people.

XUÉSHENG: Táng Xiānsheng, nín bú yào zhèiyàngr xiǎng. Wǒmen dōu xīwàng yǐhòu Zhōngguo wénxuéde qíngxing huì hǎo yìdiǎnr. Jīntian wǒ zài túshūguǎn jièle jǐběnr xīn shū, dōu shi bú cuòde. Gěi nín liúxia ba!

STUDENT: Professor Táng, don't think that way. All of us hope that the state of Chinese literature will get better in the future. I got a few new books out of the library today which are all pretty good. I'll leave them with you!
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Hǎo, yǒu shíjiān wǒ kànyikàn.
PROFESSOR TÁNG: Okay, I'll look through them when I have time.
XUÉSHENG: Wǒ zǒu le, nín duō xiūxi yìhuǐr. Zàijiàn.
STUDENT: I'm going to leave now. You get some more rest. Good-bye.
TÁNG JIÀOSHÒU: Hǎo, zài jiàn. Xièxie nǐ lái kàn wo.
PROFESSOR TÁNG: All right, good-bye. Thanks for coming to see me.
XUÉSHENG: Bú kèqi.
STUDENT: You're welcome.
